cases.sentence: В ту же ночь, откланявшись ___, Болконский ехал к армии, сам не зная, где он найдет ее, и опасаясь по дороге к Кремсу быть перехваченным французами.
cases.explain: «военному министру» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: That same night, having taken leave of the Minister of War, Bolkónski set off to rejoin the army, not knowing where he would find it and fearing to be captured by the French on the way to Krems.

cases.sentence: В Брюнне всё ___ укладывалось, и уже отправлялись тяжести в Ольмюц.
cases.explain: «придворное население» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: In Brünn everybody attached to the court was packing up, and the heavy baggage was already being dispatched to Olmütz. Near Hetzelsdorf Prince Andréy struck the high road along which the Russian army was moving with great haste and in the greatest disorder. The road was so obstructed with carts that it was impossible to get by in a carriage. Prince Andréy took a horse and a Cossack from a Cossack commander, and hungry and weary, making his way past the baggage wagons, rode in search of the commander in chief and of his own luggage. Very sinister reports of the position of the army reached him as he went along, and the appearance of the troops in their disorderly flight confirmed these rumors.

cases.sentence: Взяв у ___ лошадь и казака, князь Андрей, голодный и усталый, обгоняя обозы, ехал отыскивать главнокомандующего и свою повозку.
cases.explain: «казачьего начальника» — after the preposition «у», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

cases.sentence: На спусках и подъемах толпы делались гуще, и стоял ___ криков.
cases.explain: «непрерывный стон» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: He looked with disdain at the endless confused mass of detachments, carts, guns, artillery, and again baggage wagons and vehicles of all kinds overtaking one another and blocking the muddy road, three and sometimes four abreast. From all sides, behind and before, as far as ear could reach, there were the rattle of wheels, the creaking of carts and gun carriages, the tramp of horses, the crack of whips, shouts, the urging of horses, and the swearing of soldiers, orderlies, and officers. All along the sides of the road fallen horses were to be seen, some flayed, some not, and broken-down carts beside which solitary soldiers sat waiting for something, and again soldiers straggling from their companies, crowds of whom set off to the neighboring villages, or returned from them dragging sheep, fowls, hay, and bulging sacks. At each ascent or descent of the road the crowds were yet denser and the din of shouting more incessant. Soldiers floundering knee-deep in mud pushed the guns and wagons themselves. Whips cracked, hoofs slipped, traces broke, and lungs were strained with shouting. The officers directing the march rode backward and forward between the carts. Their voices were but feebly heard amid the uproar and one saw by their faces that they despaired of the possibility of checking this disorder.

cases.sentence: Голоса их были слабо слышны посреди ___, и по лицам их видно было, что они отчаивались в возможности остановить этот беспорядок.
cases.explain: «общего гула» — after the preposition «посреди», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

cases.sentence: «Voilà le cher[305] Вот оно милое ___» подумал Болконский, вспоминая слова Билибина.
cases.explain: «православное воинство» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Here is our dear Orthodox Russian army,” thought Bolkónski, recalling Bilíbin’s words.

cases.sentence: В экипаже правил солдат и сидела под ___ за фартуком женщина, вся обвязанная платками.
cases.explain: «кожаным верхом» — after the preposition «под», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Wishing to find out where the commander in chief was, he rode up to a convoy. Directly opposite to him came a strange one-horse vehicle, evidently rigged up by soldiers out of any available materials and looking like something between a cart, a cabriolet, and a calèche. A soldier was driving, and a woman enveloped in shawls sat behind the apron under the leather hood of the vehicle. Prince Andréy rode up and was just putting his question to a soldier when his attention was diverted by the desperate shrieks of the woman in the vehicle. An officer in charge of transport was beating the soldier who was driving the woman’s vehicle for trying to get ahead of others, and the strokes of his whip fell on the apron of the equipage. The woman screamed piercingly. Seeing Prince Andréy she leaned out from behind the apron and, waving her thin arms from under the woolen shawl, cried:

cases.sentence: Увидав князя Андрея, она высунулась из-под фартука и, махая худыми руками, выскочившими из-под ___, кричала:
cases.explain: «коврового платка» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

cases.sentence: — вдруг с ___ обратился к нему офицер.
cases.explain: «пьяным бешенством» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “And who are you?” cried the officer, turning on him with tipsy rage, “who are you? Are you in command here? Eh? I am commander here, not you! Go back or I’ll flatten you into a pancake,” repeated he. This expression evidently pleased him.

cases.sentence: Князь Андрей видел, что офицер находился в том ___ беспричинного бешенства, в котором люди не помнят, что́ говорят.
cases.explain: «пьяном припадке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Prince Andréy saw that the officer was in that state of senseless, tipsy rage when a man does not know what he is saying. He saw that his championship of the doctor’s wife in her queer trap might expose him to what he dreaded more than anything in the world—to ridicule; but his instinct urged him on. Before the officer finished his sentence Prince Andréy, his face distorted with fury, rode up to him and raised his riding whip.

cases.sentence: Въехав в деревню, он слез с лошади и пошел к ___ с намерением отдохнуть хоть на минуту, съесть что-нибудь и привесть в ясность все эти оскорбительные, мучившие его мысли.
cases.explain: «первому дому» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: On reaching the village he dismounted and went to the nearest house, intending to rest if but for a moment, eat something, and try to sort out the stinging and tormenting thoughts that confused his mind. “This is a mob of scoundrels and not an army,” he was thinking as he went up to the window of the first house, when a familiar voice called him by name.

cases.sentence: «Это толпа мерзавцев, а не войско», думал он, подходя к окну ___, когда знакомый ему голос назвал его по имени.
cases.explain: «первого дома» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

cases.sentence: Из ___ высовывалось красивое лицо Несвицкого.
cases.explain: «маленького окна» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: He turned round. Nesvítski’s handsome face looked out of the little window. Nesvítski, moving his moist lips as he chewed something, and flourishing his arm, called him to enter.

cases.explain: «сочным ртом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: He turned round. Nesvítski’s handsome face looked out of the little window. Nesvítski, moving his moist lips as he chewed something, and flourishing his arm, called him to enter.

cases.sentence: Войдя в дом, князь Андрей увидал Несвицкого и еще ___, закусывавших что-то.
cases.explain: «другого адъютанта» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Entering the house, Prince Andréy saw Nesvítski and another adjutant having something to eat. They hastily turned round to him asking if he had any news. On their familiar faces he read agitation and alarm. This was particularly noticeable on Nesvítski’s usually laughing countenance.

cases.sentence: — Теперь, князь, ни повозок, ничего не найдете, и ваш Петр Бог его знает где, — сказал ___.
cases.explain: «другой адъютант» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “You won’t be able to find either your baggage or anything else now, Prince. And God only knows where your man Pyotr is,” said the other adjutant.

cases.sentence: — Где ж ___?
cases.explain: «главная квартира» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Where are headquarters?”

cases.sentence: Хоть через ___ удирать.
cases.explain: «Богемские горы» — after the preposition «через», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Well, I have got all I need into packs for two horses,” said Nesvítski. “They’ve made up splendid packs for me—fit to cross the Bohemian mountains with. It’s a bad lookout, old fellow! But what’s the matter with you? You must be ill to shiver like that,” he added, noticing that Prince Andréy winced as at an electric shock.

cases.sentence: Он вспомнил в эту минуту о ___ с лекарскою женой и фурштатским офицером.
cases.explain: «недавнем столкновении» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: He had just remembered his recent encounter with the doctor’s wife and the convoy officer.

cases.sentence: Он вспомнил в эту минуту о недавнем столкновении с лекарскою женой и ___.
cases.explain: «фурштатским офицером» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: He had just remembered his recent encounter with the doctor’s wife and the convoy officer.

cases.sentence: Вейротер был ___, заменивший убитого Шмита.
cases.explain: «австрийский генерал» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Passing by Kutúzov’s carriage and the exhausted saddle horses of his suite, with their Cossacks who were talking loudly together, Prince Andréy entered the passage. Kutúzov himself, he was told, was in the house with Prince Bagratión and Weyrother. Weyrother was the Austrian general who had succeeded Schmidt. In the passage little Kozlóvski was squatting on his heels in front of a clerk. The clerk, with cuffs turned up, was hastily writing at a tub turned bottom upwards. Kozlóvski’s face looked worn—he too had evidently not slept all night. He glanced at Prince Andréy and did not even nod to him.

cases.sentence: Но в то время, как он хотел отворить дверь, голоса в комнате замолкли, дверь сама отворилась, и Кутузов, с своим ___ на пухлом лице, показался на пороге.
cases.explain: «орлиным носом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Prince Andréy moved toward the door from whence voices were heard. Just as he was going to open it the sounds ceased, the door opened, and Kutúzov with his eagle nose and puffy face appeared in the doorway. Prince Andréy stood right in front of Kutúzov but the expression of the commander in chief’s one sound eye showed him to be so preoccupied with thoughts and anxieties as to be oblivious of his presence. He looked straight at his adjutant’s face without recognizing him.

cases.sentence: Багратион, невысокий, с ___ твердого и неподвижного лица, сухой, еще не старый человек, вышел за главнокомандующим.
cases.explain: «восточным типом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Bagratión, a gaunt middle-aged man of medium height with a firm, impassive face of Oriental type, came out after the commander in chief.

cases.sentence: Благословляю тебя на ___.
cases.explain: «великий подвиг» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Well, goodbye, Prince,” said he to Bagratión. “My blessing, and may Christ be with you in your great endeavor!”

cases.sentence: — Садись, — сказал Кутузов и, заметив, что Болконский медлит, — мне ___ самому нужны, самому нужны.
cases.explain: «хорошие офицеры» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Get in,” said Kutúzov, and noticing that Bolkónski still delayed, he added: “I need good officers myself, need them myself!”

cases.sentence: — Еще впереди много, много всего будет, — сказал он со ___ проницательности, как будто поняв всё, что́ делалось в душе Болконского.
cases.explain: «старческим выражением» — after the preposition «со», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “There is still much, much before us,” he said, as if with an old man’s penetration he understood all that was passing in Bolkónski’s mind. “If a tenth part of his detachment returns I shall thank God,” he added as if speaking to himself.

cases.sentence: Он с тонкою насмешливостью расспрашивал князя Андрея о подробностях его свидания с императором, об отзывах, слышанных при дворе о ___, и о некоторых общих знакомых женщинах.
cases.explain: «кремском деле» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Kutúzov did not reply. He seemed to have forgotten what he had been saying, and sat plunged in thought. Five minutes later, gently swaying on the soft springs of the carriage, he turned to Prince Andréy. There was not a trace of agitation on his face. With delicate irony he questioned Prince Andréy about the details of his interview with the Emperor, about the remarks he had heard at court concerning the Krems affair, and about some ladies they both knew.
